title: Ablative Absolute
objectives: Form ablative absolutes with perfect passive participles
Form ablative absolutes with present active participles
Use ablative absolutes to express circumstance, time, cause, or concession

vocabulary.definition: the city having been captured / with the city captured
the leader coming / with the leader coming
I being unwilling / against my will
Caesar being consul / when Caesar was consul

grammar.explanation: The ablative absolute is a participial phrase grammatically independent from the main clause. It consists of a noun/pronoun in the ablative + a participle (or adjective/noun) in the ablative. It expresses time, cause, condition, or concession.
rules: The subject of the ablative absolute is NOT the subject of the main verb
Translate with: when, after, since, although, if, with
No 'being' verb in Latin; understand 'being' with adjective/noun
Perfect participle = prior action; present participle = simultaneous action

exercises.question: Translate: Hostibus victis, milites domum redierunt.
exercises.answer: The enemies having been conquered, the soldiers returned home. / After conquering the enemies, the soldiers returned home.

exercises.question: Write an ablative absolute for 'after the letter was written'

readingPassage.latin: Sole oriente, agricolae in agros exierunt. Opere confecto, domum redierunt. Patre mortuo, filius familiae praefuit. His rebus gestis, Caesar in Galliam profectus est.
readingPassage.translation: The sun rising, the farmers went out into the fields. The work having been completed, they returned home. The father having died, the son presided over the family. These things having been accomplished, Caesar set out for Gaul.
notes: These ablative absolutes show time and cause relationships
